text:
Sunset came at 4:32 this evening, and the clouds are thickening behind it as the next system slides in. We've had a dry, mild Sunday, with highs right around 50. Showers arrive after 7 or so and hang around on and off overnight. They'll be light, under a tenth of an inch, and we settle into the low 40s by morning. A light jacket will do if you're out early.

Monday is the wetter half of the pair. The best chance for showers comes through the morning commute, roughly 6 to 10, then they get patchier and wind down by mid-afternoon. Total rain is only about a tenth of an inch, with a high near 50. The models disagree a bit on how soggy it gets. One keeps it fairly dry, another is wetter, but I'd bet on a damp morning and a drier afternoon. Take the umbrella out the door, and plan any walk for after 3. Monday night turns colder, down around 35.

Tuesday brings another light round of showers by afternoon, and Wednesday dries out. Late in the week looks colder, with a possible rain and snow mix, but the track is still unsettled.

week.blurb: Mostly sunny and mild with a high near 49, then light showers arrive after 7 tonight, so grab a jacket.
Showers likely with a high around 50, light amounts, and the models disagree on how steady, so keep the umbrella close.
Dry start, then rain moves in after 10am with a high near 52, and it keeps going into the evening.
Leftover rain possible until about 1pm, then cloudy and a touch cooler, high near 49, with a chilly night near 30.
Colder and mostly cloudy with a high near 43, a stray shower possible after 1pm, then rain and snow mixing in tonight.
Looks raw and mostly cloudy with a high near 41, and a rain and snow mix is possible at times.
Trending chilly again with a high near 41, mostly cloudy skies, and a decent shot at more rain and snow mixing.

AFD DISCUSSION (the forecaster's full reasoning, same regional caveat; their temps are area-wide ranges):
KEY MESSAGE 1: A dry afternoon is expected today as low pressure shifts eastward into the Canadian Maritimes, and high pressure over the Mississippi River Valley builds into the northeastern U.S. Seasonable temperatures currently in the mid 40s to lower 50s are expected to fall as we head into the overnight hours, dropping to the mid 30s to lower 40s by early Monday morning, which is relatively mild for this time of year. West-northwesterly winds will decrease into the overnight as well, though westerly gusts may continue at higher elevations with a modest low level jet overhead. Precipitation chances also increase again this evening and tonight as we remain under the influence of a large upper level low rotating over eastern Canada. The first shortwave it sends our way will move overhead tonight and Monday. Much like our recent round of precipitation, most of the shower activity will fall as rain, with some light snow possible across the higher terrain and portions of the Adirondacks/Northeast Kingdom, especially tonight. Any snow accumulation will be minimal below 2500 ft. Rain will be the name of the game on Monday with highs in the 40s and lower 50s again. Precipitation amounts are expected to be up to 0.20" at most, highest in the northern Greens. Winds could also be slightly breezy again Monday out of the northwest, but not overly impactful. After brief ridging Monday night and lows in the mid 20s to mid 30s, the next shortwave should strike on Tuesday, though precipitation amounts are expected to be lighter, up to 0.15" at most. Once again, Tuesday's seasonable highs in the upper 40s to mid 50s will limit much snow during the day, then overnight lows in the upper 20s and 30s could allow for some light snow at higher elevations and cold spots. Tuesday's winds will be out of the southwest and slightly breezy, but again not overly impactful. On Wednesday, we'll be drying out with highs in the 40s to mid 50s and winds out of the west-northwest again. KEY MESSAGE 2: A period of unsettled weather looks to continue late next week into the weekend, with additional chances for precipitation expected. A lage-scale trough is expected to develop across the eastern CONUS, with a developing surface low centered over the Ohio Valley, with a strengthening secondary low expected to develop and move through the Mid-Atlantic towards the New England Coast. Temperatures look to trend colder towards the weekend, with highs only in the 30s and low 40s. Model guidance continues to struggle with the expected low track, which will greatly influence how much precipitation northern New York and Vermont can expect, as well as precipitation type. Guidance is still rather split on whether the low will be suppressed far enough south that we miss out or if it will bring widespread precipitation to the region, but trends generally support a wetter solution although there is still even more uncertainty regarding the expected precipitation type. WCAX METEOROLOGIST (regional station — Burlington relevance only, never their branding): BURLINGTON, Vt. (WCAX) - Any showers have ended for our region, though the outer fringes of the low pressure system are producing snow for Coos County, New Hampshire. The snow may persist until late morning or even midday, with a trace to 3 inches accumulation, though the higher amounts will be in the White Mountains. The rest of today will become partly sunny with highs in the mid-40s to low 50s. The next system will quickly move in Sunday night with more showers. Showers are likely on Monday, especially for the morning. They will become more widely scattered as the afternoon progresses. Highs will be in the 40s with lows in the 30s. Tuesday and Veterans Day looks a little drier now, though a few showers can’t be ruled out both days. Our eyes then turn to a potential coastal storm late in the week, though it can still change as the time is pretty far out. At this time, Thursday is expected to have increasing clouds with a rain/snow mix by afternoon, continuing overnight and through Friday. Some snow accumulation isn’t out of the question, even in the valleys, but there’s still plenty of time for things to change. Showers and mountain snow showers may continue into Saturday with highs mainly in the 30s and lows in the 20s. It’s something we’ll keep an eye on during the week.
NBC5 METEOROLOGIST (2026-11-08T13:52:00Z — same caveat): Seasonably cool Sunday, clouds slowly give way to sun — Sunday looks drier, though patchy drizzle and elevation snowflakes linger early. Expect stubborn clouds through the morning, but more rays of sun should mix in through the afternoon. Highs will be near 50. Clouds increase and scattered showers return this evening into tonight, as a clipper system arrives. Lows reach the 30s and 40s. Monday will be mostly cloudy and cool, as scattered showers continue. Additional mountain flakes are possible, especially for the summits. Highs reach the upper 40s, with a stiff northwest breeze. After a mostly dry start to Tuesday, another round of showers comes through by afternoon. Highs reach the low 50s. Wednesday (Veterans Day) turns drier, with only a spot shower leftover. However, it will be cloudy and cool, with highs in the upper 40s. The late-week stretch looks quite chilly, as the jet stream dips farther south. Highs will be closer to 40, with lots of clouds. A storm system may bring a round of rain and elevation snow Friday into Saturday, but uncertainty remains with the track. Stay tuned for updates.
